estimate.damage_summary: A heavy bowl was knocked into a display cabinet, cracking the cabinet-door glass and denting/gouging the solid-wood frame; the impact also scratched and chipped an internal wooden shelf. The photo is consistent with the reported damage.
estimate.policy_notes: The timber damage is plausibly sudden accidental damage under 2.6.1; ordinary-use marks are excluded by 2.6.3(a), but the described impact damage is distinct from ordinary wear. Glazing is excluded from that peril under 2.6.4 and is covered only if optional glazing is shown as agreed in the missing schedule (2.7.1, 2.7.3 and 3.5). Accordingly, the glass-related lines are treated as not covered on the information provided. Under 7.1.12, one attendance charge may be indemnified if indemnifiable timber repair was carried out on that visit; no proportional reduction or deductible is established in the material provided.

lines.rationale: Drilling is preparatory glazing work under 1.3 and 2.7.2, but it follows the glass replacement and is not covered if optional glazing was not agreed (2.7.3 and 3.5). It is related to fitting the replacement pane; one operation is plausible, with an indicative maximum reasonable net price of about €60 if the line were valid.

lines.invoice_text: Installation of the new glass into the frame
lines.rationale: Setting and fitting the pane are glazing work under 1.3 and 2.7.2, and are excluded unless the optional glazing peril is agreed (2.7.3 and 3.5). Installation is related to the cracked pane and one fitting operation is plausible; if valid, a reasonable maximum net price is about €180.

The pane is a glazing element, and its replacement is covered only if optional glazing is shown as agreed in the schedule (2.7.1, 2.7.3 and 3.5); that agreement is not provided. The pane is related to the reported breakage, and one replacement is plausible; assuming validity, the specification and dimensions are unknown, so a reasonable maximum net price could reach about €450 for a standard equivalent.

lines.invoice_text: Repair of dented and gouged solid-wood door frame
lines.rationale: Repair of the frame is plausibly covered as necessary repair of damaged household property under 2.6.1 and 7.1.1(b); the impact dents and gouges described are not ordinary-use marks under 2.6.3(a). The photo supports damage to the frame, and one localized repair and finish restoration is plausible; a reasonable maximum net flat rate is about €450, limited to the affected parts under 7.1.5 and 7.1.9.

lines.invoice_text: Repair and refinish of scratched and chipped wooden shelf
lines.rationale: The shelf repair is plausibly covered under 2.6.1 and 7.1.1(b) if the described scratches and chips were caused by this impact; ordinary-use scratching or chipping alone would be excluded by 2.6.3(a). The line is related to the reported incident, but the photo provides less clear confirmation of the shelf damage, so only localized repair and refinishing is justified under 7.1.5 and 7.1.9.

This appears to be an attendance or travel charge. Under 7.1.12, one attendance per undertaking may be paid in full if indemnifiable work, such as the timber repair, was carried out at that visit; a charge for a visit involving only excluded glazing work would not be covered. One attendance is plausible, with a reasonable maximum net charge of about €70.
